newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude; Oman steady despite narrow Dubai diff.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude; Oman steady despite narrow Dubai diff.

text.p: The Middle East market was thin, as traders considered the impact of the official prices.
Although an adjustment in the Oman official price has narrowed the crude's differential to Dubai, traders expected that the impact on spot market would be psychological.
"People perceive that Oman is coming in line with expectations and will rank Oman higher compared to alternative crudes" said a trader with a major oil company.
"But ultimately, the July Oman price will affected by the demand and supply situation. If China doesn't come out, the market will remain in the doldrums" he said.
But traders expected firmer Abu Dhabi prices following the narrower Dubai/Abu Dhabi differential since most of the July cargoes were currently held by equity producers.
Murban prices have already strengthened, with a seller expecting to get around ADNOC -15 cents per barrel, compared to the last July trade done at ADNOC -26.
Only three cargoes of Murban were heard available in July, but a need for 600kb from Kenya was likely to emerge this week.
In addition, several South Korean and Japanese refiners were heard also looking to buy July Murban.
Thin demand kept Minas trading lacklustre.
Bids for June barrels were expected to come from ICP even, with a few shosha heard offering ICP +15.
In contrast, premiums of Bach Ho crude remained firm.
A major confirmed buying a partial cargo from a shosha at OSP +48 late last week, to take to Australia.
The same major had bought a full cargo earlier last week from another shosha at OSP +45.
